title: Police probes on Island drag on
article: One hope for B.C.'s new Independent Investigations Office is that it will complete investigations in a timely manner, which is severely lacking in the current system.
It's not uncommon for probes of police-involved deaths or injuries to drag on for years, as many of the police investigators juggle the files along with many other cases.

By comparison, Ontario's Special Investigations Unit aims for a 30-day turnaround on its cases. But that goal isn't always met when it comes to more complicated shooting or death cases because investigators have to wait for pathology and toxicology tests to make their way through backlogged labs.
Investigations into three police shootings on the Island -- led by the Vancouver Island Integrated Major Crime Unit -- have eclipsed a year.
Derek Welton, 39, was shot by a veteran North Cowichan/Duncan RCMP officer on March 1, 2009, after police say he came at the officers with a knife in his trailer.

Bill Gillespie is still waiting for answers as to why an officer shot him in the neck after he was pulled over by North Cowichan/Duncan RCMP in Chemainus on Sept. 18, 2009. Gillespie says he wasn't armed and was obeying the officer's orders to kneel down.

And the investigation continues into the shooting of Nanaimo man Jeff Hughes, who police say came at them with a weapon after they responded to a noise complaint at his apartment building Oct. 23, 2009.
The RCMP says the evidence has to be examined by a use-of-force expert with an out-of-province municipal police department, which can face delays because these experts are rare.

But David Eby, executive director of the B.C. Civil Liberties Association, said it is unacceptable how long cases drag on -- prolonging a painful process for the families of the victims and the officers being investigated.

"There you've got the person who pulled the trigger, you've got the weapon, you've got the victim, you've got the crime scene and yet these investigations take years to complete," he said. "It's embarrassing for police departments, how long it takes to do these investigations when they manage to move through other investigations so quickly."
